subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 100 easy / 0 medium / 0 hard. Tier is relative: the easy third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: Myositis ossificans traumatica is most commonly associated with injury around which joint?
questions.explanation: Elbow dislocation or supracondylar fracture treated with vigorous passive stretching can cause heterotopic ossification in the brachialis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: An incentive spirometer encourages the patient to:

options.B: Take a slow, maximal sustained inspiration
options.D: Hold the breath after a short sniff

questions.explanation: Sustained maximal inspirations (SMI) improve lung volumes and prevent postoperative atelectasis.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A coupling medium (gel) is used with the ultrasound transducer in order to:

options.A: Increase the heat of the gel
options.C: Reflect the ultrasound back into the machine
options.D: Eliminate air between the transducer and the skin so the energy is transmitted

questions.explanation: Air reflects almost all ultrasound; gel (or water) ensures acoustic contact.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Derealisation and depersonalisation, when they occur as anxiety symptoms, are classified under which category of psychological symptoms?
questions.explanation: Derealisation and depersonalisation are classified as perceptual symptoms of anxiety, distinct from cognitive symptoms (poor concentration, distractibility), affective symptoms (fearfulness, apprehension), and physical/motoric symptoms (tremors, restlessness).
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.sourceChapter: Neurotic, Stress-related and Somatoform Disorders — Anxiety Disorder, Symptoms
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: Stable angina pectoris is typically:

options.A: Chest pain on exertion relieved by rest or nitrates within minutes

questions.explanation: Due to myocardial ischaemia from fixed coronary stenosis.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: In a three-pin mains plug, the earth pin is made longer and thicker than the live and neutral pins so that:

options.A: It prevents the plug from being inserted the wrong way round only
options.B: It connects last so that the live pin is always energised first
options.C: It carries the main treatment current to the patient
options.D: It connects first when plugged in and disconnects last when removed

questions.explanation: The longer, thicker earth pin makes contact before the live and neutral pins and breaks last, so the metal casing is earthed whenever the apparatus is live. Its shape also stops the plug being inserted wrongly.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Percussion (clapping) over the chest wall is performed with:

options.A: Cupped hands in a rhythmic manner over the segment being drained
options.D: A closed fist directly on the spine

questions.explanation: A cupped hand traps air and produces a gentle wave; avoid bony prominences, breasts and the kidney area.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Asthma is characterised by:

options.C: Reversible airflow obstruction with wheeze, cough and breathlessness

questions.explanation: Bronchial hyper-reactivity and inflammation; PEFR shows diurnal variation >20%.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Claw hand (main en griffe) is characteristic of an:
questions.explanation: Paralysed ulnar-supplied lumbricals/interossei leave the ring and little finger MCP hyperextended with IP flexion; the deformity is worse in a low lesion because FDP is intact.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The common peroneal nerve winds around the:
questions.explanation: It divides into superficial and deep peroneal nerves; injury causes foot drop.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The Modified Ashworth Scale is used to grade:
questions.explanation: Graded 0–4 (with 1+): resistance to passive movement. It does not measure strength.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: During diaphragmatic breathing the abdomen should:

options.B: Rise on inspiration and fall on expiration

questions.explanation: Diaphragm descends on inspiration, pushing abdominal contents outward.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The most common cause of wrist drop is injury to the:

options.C: Radial nerve in the spiral groove (e.g. humeral shaft fracture)
options.D: Median nerve at the carpal tunnel

questions.explanation: Radial nerve palsy leaves the wrist and finger extensors paralysed; a cock-up splint maintains the wrist in extension.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Autonomic dysreflexia occurs in spinal cord injuries at or above:
questions.explanation: A noxious stimulus below the lesion (bladder distension, bowel loading, pressure sore) triggers uncontrolled sympathetic outflow with severe hypertension, headache and bradycardia.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The normal motor nerve conduction velocity in the upper limb is approximately:
questions.explanation: Upper limb motor conduction velocity is typically 50–70 m/s; lower limb values are lower (about 40–50 m/s) and decrease with cooling and age.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Erb's palsy results from injury to the:

options.C: Upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)

questions.explanation: Upper trunk injury (birth traction injury) produces the ‘waiter's tip’ posture: arm adducted, medially rotated, elbow extended and forearm pronated.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which muscle is the strongest flexor of the elbow regardless of forearm position?
questions.explanation: Brachialis attaches to the ulna so is unaffected by forearm rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Most nutrient absorption in the gastrointestinal tract occurs in the:
questions.explanation: The surface area is greatly increased by villi and microvilli.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Barlow's provocative test and Ortolani's test are used to detect:

options.A: Developmental dysplasia (instability) of the hip in infants

questions.explanation: Ortolani reduces a dislocated hip with a ‘clunk’ (abduct and lift); Barlow dislocates an unstable hip (adduct and push).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A 10-RM refers to the:

options.A: Weight that can be lifted once
options.C: Maximum load a muscle can move through the full range exactly 10 times

questions.explanation: The repetition maximum concept was introduced by DeLorme. 1-RM is the heaviest load for a single full-range repetition.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: ORS stands for:
questions.explanation: Low-osmolarity ORS is the treatment of choice for dehydration in diarrhoea, together with zinc.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The unique sequence of amino acids in a protein, determined by the genes in DNA, is called its:
questions.explanation: The primary structure of a protein is its specific linear sequence of amino acids, determined by the genetic code. It is largely responsible for the protein's function, and a large number of genetic diseases arise from abnormalities in this amino acid sequence.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Primary Structure
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: The principal muscle of quiet inspiration is the:
questions.explanation: Contraction flattens the dome, increasing the vertical thoracic dimension. Quiet expiration is passive.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: In congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) the foot is held in:

options.A: Plantar flexion, inversion and forefoot adduction

questions.explanation: CTEV: equinus (plantar flexion) of the hindfoot, varus (inversion) of the heel and adduction of the forefoot, with a cavus arch (CAVE).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The ground reaction force during walking is an example of Newton's:
questions.explanation: When the foot pushes on the ground, the ground pushes back with an equal and opposite force.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A therapist treating a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis should use:

options.B: A properly fitted N95/FFP2 respirator (airborne precautions)

questions.explanation: TB spreads by airborne droplet nuclei; airborne isolation with N95 masks is required.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The X-ray appearance classically described in giant cell tumour of bone is:
questions.explanation: Osteosarcoma: sunburst; Ewing's sarcoma: onion peel; fibrous dysplasia: ground glass.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Dreaming occurs mainly in:
questions.explanation: Paradoxical sleep with rapid eye movements and loss of muscle tone.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The Berg Balance Scale has a maximum score of:
questions.explanation: 14 items each scored 0–4; scores <45 suggest fall risk.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A hard (bone-to-bone) end-feel is normal at the end of:
questions.explanation: Olecranon contacting the olecranon fossa produces a hard end-feel at full elbow extension.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Which is the first functional task usually taught to a patient with a thoracic spinal cord injury?
questions.explanation: Bed mobility, then sitting balance, transfers, wheelchair skills and later gait.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Permanent dilatation of the medium-sized bronchi with recurrent infection and copious purulent sputum is:
questions.explanation: Bronchiectasis causes chronic productive cough; treatment includes postural drainage and ACBT; HRCT is diagnostic.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: TENS should NOT be applied:

options.A: For post-operative wound pain at a distance from the wound
options.B: Over the carotid sinus or in a patient with a demand-type cardiac pacemaker
options.D: For pain in labour on the lower back

questions.explanation: Absolute cautions for TENS: demand pacemakers, over the carotid sinus, over the anterior neck, eyes, pregnant uterus (except back in labour), and areas of impaired sensation or thrombosis.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The anterior drawer test of the knee primarily assesses:
questions.explanation: With the knee at 90° flexion, anterior translation of the tibia on the femur >6–8 mm beyond the other side indicates ACL laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The first action when a tetraplegic patient develops autonomic dysreflexia in the wheelchair is to:

options.C: Sit the patient upright, loosen tight clothing, check bladder/bowel and call for medical help

questions.explanation: Sitting upright reduces blood pressure; then remove the trigger (usually catheter blockage or faecal loading).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Neural tube defects can be significantly reduced by maternal supplementation of:
questions.explanation: 400 µg daily (4 mg in high risk) before conception and through the first trimester.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The cardinal features of Parkinson's disease are:

options.A: Resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and postural instability

questions.explanation: Degeneration of the substantia nigra reduces dopamine; tremor is pill-rolling at 4–6 Hz at rest.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which agent is commonly used for skin preparation before surgery?
questions.explanation: Skin preparation reduces surgical site infection.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The most specific biochemical marker for myocardial infarction is:
questions.explanation: Troponin rises within 3–6 hours and stays elevated for 7–14 days; CK-MB is a secondary marker.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Malignant tumours arising from epithelial tissue are generally named:
questions.explanation: Malignant tumours of epithelial origin are called carcinomas, while malignant tumours of mesenchymal (connective tissue) origin are called sarcomas.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Muscle hypertrophy is mainly due to:

options.B: Increase in the size (cross-sectional area) of existing muscle fibres
options.C: Increase in the number of fibres

questions.explanation: Resistance training increases myofibril number and protein content within fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The Milwaukee brace is used in:
questions.explanation: The Milwaukee brace is a cervico-thoraco-lumbo-sacral orthosis used for high thoracic curves in scoliosis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Trigger finger (stenosing tenosynovitis) is most commonly associated with:
questions.explanation: Nodule in the flexor tendon catches at the A1 pulley.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Continuous Passive Motion (CPM) is best described as:

options.A: An exercise in which the patient actively moves a joint against resistance
options.B: A mechanical device that moves a joint slowly and continuously through a controlled range of motion, without effort from the patient
options.C: A manual stretching technique applied by the therapist at end-range
options.D: A functional movement pattern combining several joints at once

questions.explanation: CPM refers specifically to a mechanical device that passively and continuously moves a joint through a set arc of motion, developed following Robert Salter's research into the healing benefits of continual passive movement on joint tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 3: Range of Motion — Continuous Passive Motion
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: A thyroid swelling moves upward with swallowing because it:

options.C: Is attached to the pretracheal fascia

questions.explanation: A thyroglossal cyst also moves on tongue protrusion.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: In the neutral zero method of recording joint range, the anatomical position is taken as:

options.A: 0° for all joints (except forearm in mid-rotation)

questions.explanation: The neutral zero method (Cave and Roberts) records all motion from the anatomical position, so normal extension of the elbow is 0° and flexion 135–150°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Ultrasound intensity is expressed in:
questions.explanation: Intensity = power (W) / effective radiating area (cm²). Typical therapeutic range is 0.1–2.0 W/cm².
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The most effective reversible contraceptive method with a failure rate below 1% is:
questions.explanation: Combined oral pills have a typical-use failure rate of about 7–9%.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Community-based rehabilitation (CBR) aims to:

options.D: Ensure that people with disabilities can access rehabilitation, equal opportunities and social inclusion within their own community

questions.explanation: The CBR matrix has five components: health, education, livelihood, social and empowerment.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: During muscle contraction, the sarcomere shortens because:

options.D: Actin filaments slide over myosin filaments, shortening the I-band and H-zone

questions.explanation: The A-band length stays constant.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A complete tear of a ligament is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Grade I: stretch with minimal fibre damage; grade II: partial tear; grade III: complete rupture with instability. Strain refers to muscle/tendon.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox after a fall on the outstretched hand suggests a fracture of the:
questions.explanation: The scaphoid forms the floor of the anatomical snuffbox. Initial X-rays may be normal, so scaphoid precautions and repeat imaging are used.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: SBAR, a structured communication tool used for handovers and referrals, stands for:
questions.explanation: SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) is a structured communication framework recommended for handovers and referrals, increasing the amount of relevant clinical information communicated in a short time.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Effective Team Communication
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The Gestalt law of 'proximity' states that:

options.A: Items that are close together in space or time tend to be perceived as belonging together, forming a group
options.B: Only identical items can ever be grouped together
options.C: Distant objects are always perceived as larger
options.D: Proximity has no influence on perceptual grouping

questions.explanation: The law of proximity states that items close together in space or time tend to be perceived as belonging together or forming an organized group — for example, seeing three pairs of lines rather than six separate lines when they are grouped closely.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Sensory Processes and Perception — Organization in Perception
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: The commonest type of cerebral palsy is:
questions.explanation: Spastic CP (~70–80%) includes diplegia, hemiplegia and quadriplegia; athetoid ~10–20%.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The mitral valve lies between the:
questions.explanation: Mitral (bicuspid) valve prevents backflow into the left atrium; tricuspid is on the right.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The best method of disposal of excreta in rural areas without sewerage is:
questions.explanation: Sanitation breaks the faecal–oral transmission of cholera, typhoid and hookworm.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Which component of the quadriceps also acts as a hip flexor?
questions.explanation: It is the only biarticular head, crossing the hip and knee.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Lesions of one cerebellar hemisphere produce symptoms:
questions.explanation: Intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, nystagmus and hypotonia.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Hypertension in adults is defined as a sustained blood pressure of:
questions.explanation: Stage 1 hypertension (ACC/AHA 2017 uses ≥130/80); malignant hypertension has papilloedema.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The ankle jerk is mainly mediated by which spinal segment?
questions.explanation: Knee jerk L3–L4; ankle jerk S1; biceps jerk C5–C6; triceps C7; supinator C5–C6.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The musculocutaneous nerve supplies:
questions.explanation: It pierces coracobrachialis; ends as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Duchenne muscular dystrophy follows which pattern of inheritance?
questions.explanation: Boys are affected; onset 3–5 years; wheelchair dependence by about 12 years; death from respiratory or cardiac failure.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences
